newsitem.title: USA: Fed okays Bankers Trust bid for Alex. Brown.
newsitem.headline: Fed okays Bankers Trust bid for Alex. Brown.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Board said Monday it approved a bid by Bankers Trust New York Corp. to acquire 100 percent of the voting shares of Alex. Brown Inc..

Under the $1.7 billion stock swap merger announced on April 6, Bankers Trust would engage in a variety of nonbanking activities, including underwriting and dealing in all types of debt and equity securities on a limited basis, the Fed said.

Bankers Trust, with assets of $120.2 billion, would acquire Baltimore-based Alex. Brown, with $2.5 billion in assets, by merging its Alex. Brown & Sons Inc. subsidiary into the bank holding company's securities subsidiary.

The Fed said it found that the securities activities of Alex. Brown that Bankers Trust would acquire are closely related to banking and therefore permissible under the 1933 Glass-Steagall Act, which limits the type of securities services in which banks may engage.

It said Bankers Trust has committed to abide by a Fed determination that the company engaged in the underwriting and dealing may derive no more than 25 percent of its total gross revenue over any two-year period from those activities.

The merger would not result in undue concentration of resources, decreased or unfair competition, conflicts of interest or unsound banking practices that would outweigh public benefits, it said. Services Alex. Brown provides to mutual funds are permissible under Glass-Steagall, it added.

"The Board expects that the proposed acquisition would provide added convenience to customers of (Bankers Trust) and Alex. Brown, including Alex. Brown's current mutual fund clients," the Fed said in its 13-page order.
